claims.title: Autonomous quantum memory: logical safety, a universal finite-device lifetime ceiling and the open threshold

quoted_fields.interface: Every finite autonomous device on n fixed-dimensional sites, including all controllers/ancillas/resets, complete nominal local GKLS generator with ||L0||diamond<=J n,J>=1 constant. Arbitrary encoding and decoding channels, reference-safe unhalved logical-qubit diamond error, and permitted per-site HP/TA perturbation budget0<epsilon<=1.
quoted_fields.failure: The central non-equilibrium unsafe-occupation bound must hold for the COMPLETE paid perturbed generator; equilibrium Peierls suppression does not establish it. Added depolarization generally destroys Gibbs stationarity even at zero perturbation. Imported passive-memory and asynchronous-classical comparisons retain only their supplied stated scopes; no new original-body acquisition or generic thermal-to-arbitrary-GKLS transfer. No positive full threshold/no-go or new independent Capital audit. CONTINUATION: The full model permits this particular depolarizing perturbation, so the bound is genuinely model-wide for finite devices, but exp[O(n log(n/epsilon))] can exceed the desired exp(cL^a) for polynomial n(L). It therefore does not refute the target. Existing asynchronous/classical/CSS/thermal premises retain their scoped hypotheses; paid CP clocks do not establish bounded semantic damage or quantum fault containment. Robust unsafe occupation and noisy native encoded boundaries remain unconstructed. Root35–45 assessment applies to22C, not automatically to this new5C5 proof.
